options.text: The currency will appreciate, and net exports will decrease.
options.why: Foreign investors demand more of the country's currency to buy its financial assets, so the demand for the currency shifts to the right. The currency appreciates. When the currency appreciates, the country's goods become more expensive to foreigners and imports become cheaper, so net exports fall.

options.text: The currency will appreciate, and net exports will not change.
options.why: Says net exports would not change, but it would decrease. When the currency appreciates, the country's goods become more expensive to foreigners and imports become cheaper, so net exports fall.

options.text: The currency will depreciate, and net exports will decrease.
options.why: Says the value of the currency would decrease, but it would increase. Foreign investors demand more of the country's currency to buy its financial assets, so the demand for the currency shifts to the right. The currency appreciates.

options.text: The currency will appreciate, and net exports will increase.
options.why: Says net exports would increase, but it would decrease. When the currency appreciates, the country's goods become more expensive to foreigners and imports become cheaper, so net exports fall.

options.text: The currency will stay the same, and net exports will decrease.
options.why: Says the value of the currency would not change, but it would increase. Foreign investors demand more of the country's currency to buy its financial assets, so the demand for the currency shifts to the right. The currency appreciates.

options.why: Assumes any change to a single input removes capacity for both goods in this way.

options.text: The PPC pivots outward along the capital goods axis only.
options.why: Assumes a technology that helps one good moves the other axis intercept as well.
